references.text: The Lord warns that Israel will flee before their enemies if they do not keep His commands, a parallel to the consequences of disobedience in Joshua 7:12.
The command to completely destroy what was devoted to destruction, which Israel broke through Achan's sin.
The Lord warns that disobedience will lead to defeat by enemies, just as Israel experienced at Ai.
Joshua's original command regarding the devoted things at Jericho, which Achan broke and caused God's wrath.
The introduction to this event where Achan's sin with the devoted things is described.
Continuation of the Lord's speech where the people are commanded to consecrate themselves and remove what was devoted to destruction.
In the time of the judges, the pattern repeated: the Lord's anger led to Israel being handed over to their enemies.
Isaiah explains that sin separates the people from God, explaining why the Lord would no longer be with Israel.
